cards.explanation: The answer is towns. Solomon, Israel's king, gave twenty towns in the land of Galilee to Hiram king of Tyre, who had supplied him with cedar and cypress logs and gold (1 Kings 9:11). Most folks hand over a gift card, friends. Solomon handed over a whole map.

The answer is False. Hiram king of Tyre went out to inspect the towns, and the text says he was not pleased with them (1 Kings 9:12). His own words are, “What are these towns you have given me, my brother?” (1 Kings 9:13). Twenty towns, and he still wasn't pleased.

The answer is the non-Israelites still in the land. Solomon conscripted the descendants of the Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites, Hivites and Jebusites, the people who were not Israelites and who remained in the land (1 Kings 9:20-21). The Israelites had been unable to devote them to destruction. The text says they were forced laborers "…to this day." (1 Kings 9:21)

The answer is that they are his men of war and commanders. Solomon did not consign any of the Israelites to slavery, because they were his men of war, his servants, his officers, his captains, and the commanders of his chariots and cavalry (1 Kings 9:22). That's a whole leadership roster, friends.

The answer is True. The Israelites were also the chief officers over Solomon's projects, with 550 supervisors over the people who did the work (1 Kings 9:23). Those same Israelites were his men of war, his servants, his officers, his captains, and the commanders of his chariots and cavalry (1 Kings 9:22). That's a lot of clipboards, bakers.

The answer is Pharaoh's daughter. As soon as she came up from the City of David to the palace Solomon had built for her, he built the supporting terraces (1 Kings 9:24). The text already calls her Solomon's wife back in verse 16. A new palace and then terraces. That's a man who finishes the job, friends.

The answer is three. Three times a year Solomon offered burnt offerings and peace offerings on the altar he had built for the LORD, burning incense with them before the LORD (1 Kings 9:25). The verse closes with "So he completed the temple." Three times a year is a rhythm I could keep on my calendar, bakers.

The answer is Hiram king of Tyre. He sent his servants, sailors who knew the sea, to serve in the fleet with Solomon's servants (1 Kings 9:27). Remember, he's the man who supplied the cedar, cypress and gold. That's a king who sends help when a fleet needs sailors, friends.

The answer is Ophir. Hiram's sailors and Solomon's servants sailed there and imported gold, 420 talents of it, and delivered it to Solomon (1 Kings 9:28). Sailing for gold makes me feel small, friends, since I once walked across the counter for a sprinkle and thought I'd done something big.
